title.narrative: Emergency Relief and Recovery for Crisis-Affected Communities in South Sudan

description.narrative: Following the conflict crisis of 15th December 2013, which displaced tens of thousands of families inside and outside South Sudan, Caritas South Sudan (CSS) with CAFOD funding started an emergency response project which supported IDPs with construction of latrines and food aid. CSS was engaged in further or subsequent rapid assessments and identified needs of IDPs and returnees is a number of the following counties/payam locations in Central Equatoria state: Kajo Keji county (town and Liwolo payam), Yei county (town, Lasu and Tore payams) and Lainya county (Lainya and Mukaya payams). A total of 37,157 individuals (IDPs and returnees) are targeted. Of these 22,294 persons will be female and 14,863 males. Caritas South Sudan (CSS) seeks to support these vulnerable people through provision of food aid, clean drinking water, emergency shelter materials, agriculture inputs (seeds and tools), public health/hygiene promotion and support to health care and psycho-social support to increase their resilience in the face of looming hunger gap and susceptibility to increased incidences of weather related diseases during the coming rainy season; especially towards March/April. These disaster-affected people (IDPs and returnees) have also lost homes and livelihood assets, especially women will be supported, but men will also benefit from the project. The wider target host community members (about 61,657 people) will benefit indirectly through the hygiene awareness and promotion activities and from the rehabilitation of water sources e.g. digging shallow wells, protecting spring wells, repair of hand pumps. The project implementation, by CSS will be directly supported by the County RRC in Kajo Keji, Yei and Lainya counties. Whereas the beneficiaries will also be involved in project implementation e.g. through distribution committees, local leaders mobilizing people to participate in hygiene promotion awareness through messaging etc.
